sentences[0].whyEn: The HOW (the method): indem — 'by cooking myself'.
sentences[1].whyEn: The RESULT: sodass — first rain, then the closure.
sentences[3].whyEn: Degree + result split up: so müde, dass …
sentences[5].whyEn: Result: sodass wir den Zug verpassten.
sentences[7].whyEn: so + adjective, dass + result: so langweilig, dass wir gingen.
sentences[8].whyEn: Method: indem er viel gelesen hat.
sentences[9].whyEn: Result: sodass ich nicht schlafen konnte.
sentences[11].whyEn: so schnell, dass niemand sie verstand.
sentences[12].whyEn: Method: indem ich zu Fuß gehe.
sentences[13].whyEn: Result: sodass wir nach Hause gingen.
sentences[15].whyEn: so aufgeregt, dass … — degree before the adjective, result in the dass-clause.
sentences[17].whyEn: Method: indem man das Licht ausmacht.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: We protect the climate by using less energy.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: You learn a language by speaking it.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Listening is how he improves, the means, so it is indem, written as one word.
help.tips[0].en.text: Ich spare Geld, indem ich selbst koche. Sie bleibt fit, indem sie Rad fährt. Wie? → indem. Verb at the end; the same subject in both clauses (or man).
help.tips[0].en.title: indem = by …-ing (means)
help.tips[0].en.trap: 'by cooking' has no subject; German must add one: indem ich koche. And indem is not 'in dem' (in which): das Haus, in dem ich wohne.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: He practised a lot, so he passed the exam.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: It rained heavily, so the road was closed.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: Missing the appointment is the result, and the verb is at the end, so it needs sodass. deshalb would need the verb second.
help.tips[1].en.text: Der Bus kam zu spät, sodass wir den Zug verpassten. Es war laut, sodass ich nicht schlafen konnte. The result follows; verb at the end. sodass and so dass are both accepted spellings.
help.tips[1].en.title: sodass = with the result that
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: She spoke so fast that nobody understood her.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: The film was so boring that we left.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: so already stands before the adjective, so only dass follows the comma.
help.tips[2].en.text: Er war so müde, dass er einschlief. Der Film war so langweilig, dass wir gingen. When the cause is a degree (so tired, so boring), split it: so before the adjective, dass after the comma.
help.tips[2].en.title: so + adjective, dass …
help.tips[3].examples[1].en: The bus was late, so we missed the train.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: The verb blieben comes straight after the gap, in position 2, so you need the adverb deshalb. sodass would send it to the end.
help.tips[3].en.text: Es regnete, sodass die Straße gesperrt wurde. = Es regnete, deshalb wurde die Straße gesperrt. Same result, subordinate (verb last) vs main clause (verb second).
help.tips[3].en.title: sodass looks forward; deshalb looks the same way with verb second
help.context.en: You can save a lot of money by cooking yourself and ordering less. Last year I started cooking ahead every Sunday, so that I don't lose any time during the week. At first I was so unpractised that everything took twice as long. Today I manage it by choosing simple recipes – and I eat so well that I never want to order again.
help.mistakes[0].whyEn: Means with a verb needs an indem-clause.
help.mistakes[1].whyEn: With so before the adjective, use dass.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: sodass sends the verb to the end.
help.hookEn: Explain how you manage things and what follows from them: indem for 'by doing', sodass for 'and so'.
help.introEn: Two more subordinators, for how and with what result. indem answers Wie? — by doing what: Ich spare Geld, indem ich selbst koche (by cooking myself); Man lernt eine Sprache, indem man sie spricht. English uses 'by + -ing'; German uses a full clause with the verb at the end and the same subject on both sides. sodass (also written so dass) gives the consequence: Es regnete stark, sodass die Straße gesperrt wurde (so that / with the result that). When the cause is an adjective or adverb, the so moves in front of it and dass follows: Er war so müde, dass er einschlief. These two, with damit and um … zu, weil and obwohl, complete the core set of adverbial clauses; whenever you suggest a solution, indem shines — 'Man kann das Problem lösen, indem man …' is the standard proposal sentence.
help.rememberEn[0]: indem = by doing (how); sodass = with the result that.
help.rememberEn[1]: so + adjective, dass: split the so.
